reason: walk() returns null for a null or undefined value whether or not an int node is nullable: nullable only skips miss(), and miss() itself returns null and counts nothing for null and undefined; every other value is judged by the range test first, so the default changes no output and no redaction count.

In the id case a null value is returned as null when the node is nullable and otherwise goes through miss(), which also returns null and counts nothing for null; a non-null invalid id is refused either way (the second branch needs value === null), so the flag changes no output and no count (tests: an invalid result id is null and counts once).
The bool case of walk() is `typeof value === 'boolean' ? value : miss()` and never reads node.nullable, so the flag on the checked field is unused and changing it changes nothing.

Same as the other nullable ints: null yields null with no count whether or not the node is nullable (miss() counts only values that are neither null nor undefined); a present invalid audit sequence is refused and counted once either way, which tests/redact.test.cjs pins with the value 'x'.

value.split(secret).join(MASK) on a text that does not contain the secret returns the text unchanged (split gives one element and join of one element is that element), and a registered secret is never empty (six characters at least), so skipping the includes test changes no result.

parseConnection reads only the keys Server, Database, User Id and Password, all longer than one character; a pair whose '=' sits at index 1 (a one-character key) can only be replaced by the empty pair, which nothing reads, so no returned field changes (tests: a pair whose key is a single character is ignored).

Same argument as the previous entry: raising the bound from 1 to 2 only changes the pairs whose '=' sits at index 1, that is one-character keys, and none of the four keys parseConnection reads is one.

The epoch of a freshly stored item is only compared with redactor.epoch(), which starts at 0 and only grows; -1 and -2 are both different from every real epoch, so the item is published on its first read either way.
splice(0, length - RING) with length not above RING has a count of zero or less and removes nothing, so running it when the ring is within its bound is a no-op.
At length === RING the splice count length - RING is 0 and removes nothing: the two conditions differ only where the body is a no-op.

The epoch of a fresh slot is only compared with redactor.epoch(), which starts at 0 and only grows; -1 and -2 are both different from every real epoch, so the slot is published on its first read either way.

route() has just set ctx.role from the same request headers with the same authenticate() call (null when it throws), and read() only reaches this line when that call did not throw; if the token expired between the two calls read() throws before the line, so the assignment always writes the value already there.

failClosed() has exactly two call sites: the listening listener, which runs before any connection can exist so broken is still null, and the connection listener, which calls it only under broken === null; so inside failClosed the variable is null on every call and the forced condition is the real one.

When broken is already set, a repeated failClosed() only writes the same constant again and its warning is guarded by broken === null, and the next statement destroys the socket whenever broken is set: warning once and destroyed sockets are identical with or without the guard.
